raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Python's streaming chat and completions return the request's `kv_transfer_params` on the chunk that carries `finish_reason` (vllm-project/vllm#40186), as the non-streaming responses already did, so a P/D proxy can stream and still get the transfer handle. The Rust stream response types had no such field, so streaming dropped it. This PR adds it. ## Claims - Rust streaming chat and completions put `kv_transfer_params` on the finish chunk, taken from the terminal event. The usage chunk and every other chunk leave it unset, as in Python. - Non-streaming responses are unchanged. ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2312 tests run: 2312 passed, 13 skipped ``` - `chunk_stream_puts_kv_transfer_params_on_finish_chunk_only` (chat) and `completion_stream_puts_kv_transfer_params_on_finish_chunk_only` (completions) drive the real chunk streams with a terminal event carrying params, then check the serialized JSON: only the finish chunk has the key. Both fail with the assignment removed. - `completion_chunk_stream_hides_internal_prompt_only_token` (`echo` with `max_tokens=0`) now also asserts the params on its finish chunk, covering the prompt-only terminal branch; it fails with forwarding removed in that branch only. ## Details Rust already carries the value to both stream handlers (`ChatEvent::Done.kv_transfer_params`, `Finished.kv_transfer_params`). This PR adds `kv_transfer_params: Option` to `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` and `CompletionStreamResponse`, and each stream's `final_chunk` sets it. The value is per-protocol response serialization, so the change stays in `vllm-server`'s stream types and terminal-chunk builders; nothing below the server changes. Known difference: Python constructs every content chunk with `kv_transfer_params=None` set explicitly, so under `exclude_unset` the non-final chunks carry `"kv_transfer_params": null`. Rust stream chunks skip `None` fields (as they already do for `finish_reason`), so the key is absent there. This PR does not change the stream types' null-key policy. No Python test pins the streaming field (vllm-project/vllm#40186 added none). The multiturn disaggregation proxy example reads it from streamed JSON. Not a duplicate: no open PR adds `kv_transfer_params` to the Rust stream responses. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2SEJPm2Mawmm6pu8m9E1o ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
